attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Adding 'US' fits the Washington context. The proposition keeps both parts: officials no longer voice concern, and they downplay the risks.

contract.note: Reading it as a broad trend in Washington rhetoric is fair. Scoring the 'anymore' cessation part separately from downplaying follows his categorical wording. The Jan 20 to May 16, 2025 period is a reasonable reading.

evidence.note: Vance's Feb 11, 2025 Paris speech, reproduced in full, dismisses 'hand-wringing about safety' and puts building first. This is downplaying by a top official.

Fed Governor Barr's April 17, 2025 speech warns of substantive deepfake fraud risk. This contradicts the claim that concern stopped. It is an official speech, mislabelled as a news report, and comes from an independent agency.

reviews.rationale: The downplaying part holds: the Vice President openly subordinated safety to development. The claim that officials no longer voice concern does not fully hold: a sitting Fed governor publicly warned of AI-enabled fraud within the period, which the contract treats as contradicting cessation. Mixed: downplaying supported, cessation contradicted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Dating it to 2023 matches the hearing context. 'Water down' and 'lobbying' are kept.

contract.note: Reading 'even as' as the May 2023 episode, and 'water down' as seeking fewer obligations, is an ordinary and fair reading.

evidence.note: Primary text of Altman's May 16, 2023 written testimony backing regulation. It is posted by OpenAI, but it records what he said, so it is usable.
TIME, May 2023: Altman met EU regulators and objected to the 'high risk' designation that would add safety duties for OpenAI's models.
TechCrunch, May 2023, reproduces OpenAI's EU register entry showing lobbying contacts on the AI Act.

reviews.rationale: Altman's testimony backed regulation. In the same month, OpenAI met EU officials and argued against the high-risk classification that would have imposed extra obligations on its models, and its lobbying register lists the AI Act. That is advocacy for reduced obligations during the same episode. No counterevidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: All three parts are kept, along with 'concretely implemented' and 'no longer'. 'US' fits the context.

contract.note: Reading 'national AI agency' as a regulator, and requiring deterioration for 'no longer', is fair. Whether voluntary international arrangements count as governance is an interpretation he did not supply, and it decides the first part.

evidence.note: Voluntary HAIP reporting from Feb to April 2025. It shows some operating international arrangement but no binding governance. Its weight depends on interpretation.
Planned CISA cuts reported April 30, 2025. They were not completed, and no capability assessment is given for AI cybercrime.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no evidence on whether a US AI regulator existed. Its cybercrime evidence covers proposed cuts, not measured capacity or deterioration. Whether the international part holds depends on whether voluntary HAIP reporting counts. No part is settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. 'By many accounts' points to reports, but he endorses the claim.

semantics.note: The 'by many accounts' qualifier and the word 'exploded' are restored. The qualifier attributes the claim to reports; it is not a probability hedge, so the claim is a scoreable observation.

contract.note: Reading 'exploded' as sharp growth across multiple accounts, and 'coherent' as coordinated efforts, is ordinary. Since he gave no criteria for 'coherent', that reading decides the result.

evidence.note: Sumsub vendor data shows a 4x rise in detected deepfakes from 2023 to 2024. One sharp-growth account, worldwide and covering attempts only.
FinCEN alert, Nov 2024: an unquantified rise in deepfake fraud reports, plus guidance. Shows federal activity, not whether the response was coherent.
FBI notice, Dec 2024: says AI scales up fraud and gives prevention advice. Federal activity, with no assessment of coordination.

reviews.rationale: Growth is partly supported: one vendor reports a 4x rise, and FinCEN and the FBI describe increases without figures. Federal responses existed, but nothing in the packet shows whether they were coordinated by May 16, 2025, either way. The contract needs both parts, so the outcome is unresolved.
